newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Hints at reduced forward cover ruffle SAfrica rand.
newsitem.headline: Hints at reduced forward cover ruffle SAfrica rand.

text.p: Indications that the government might accelerate the Reserve Bank's withdrawal from the forward foreign exchange market ruffled the rand on Friday, dealers and analysts said.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel told a conference he had appointed a committee of Reserve Bank and finance department officials to investigate the provision of forward cover in the foreign exchange market, in view of heavy losses this year.

"Billions of rands was added to the government's debt portfolio in the process mostly without a proper public debate being had about the matter. The government cannot allow this situation to continue," he said.
His comments helped push the rand back through the 4.70 level on Friday afternoon as dealers worried that the investigation might result in curbs on Reserve Bank intervention in the forward market.
Nick Barnardt, economist at BOE NatWest, noted that one important way in which the central bank had protected the rand this year had been via intervention in the forward market.
By selling dollars forward, the Bank stopped forward rand rates from falling too far, which implicitly supported the spot rate.
Manuel said the main focus of the investigation would be directed at the long-term forward cover component.

The Reserve Bank's stated aim is to withdraw gradually from the forward forex market. But that plan had been disrupted by the fall in the rand this year which triggered a scramble for cover that could only be met by the central bank.
Bank Governor Chris Stals said at the end of August that the Bank's net oversold foreign exchange position had risen by then to over $15 billion from $8.1 in February.
Economists said it may well have risen further since then in view of the latest sell-off in the currency in October which took the rand to an all-time low of 4.77 against the dollar.
The rand was last trading at 4.7020/60.
